Where to Stay in Phuket?
12 Hotels We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Twelve Phuket hotels across every budget — 5-star beachfront pool villas down to an Old Town hostel from ฿270/night. Covering the main areas: Patong, Karon-Kata, Surin Beach, Bang Tao/Laguna, Kamala, Rawai, and Phuket Old Town. Starting from around ฿270–15,000/night.
introH2: 🏖️ Why does choosing the right beach and area in Phuket matter?
introHtml: Phuket is a big island, and the distance between beaches is further than most people expect — Patong is the liveliest beach, packed with nightlife and shops · Karon-Kata is quieter and family-friendly · Surin Beach and Bang Tao/Laguna in the north are the quiet luxury-resort zone · Kamala is a small, calm beach · Rawai-Nai Harn in the far south suits longer stays · and Phuket Old Town is inland, full of Sino-Portuguese shophouses and great food. Many travellers book without checking which beach, then spend an hour each way crossing the island. This guide brings together 12 Phuket hotels we've reviewed across every tier — drawing on real guest reviews, with prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Phuket has no metro — getting around means a rental car, scooter, taxi, or Grab (which can be hard to hail and pricier than in major cities). From Phuket Airport (HKT) in the north of the island, Patong is about 45 minutes to an hour, Karon-Kata around an hour, while Surin Beach and Bang Tao are closer to the airport. The main beach areas in this guide: Patong — lively, nightlife, shopping · Karon-Kata — long beaches, quieter, family-friendly · Surin Beach / Bang Tao / Laguna — luxury resorts, calm and quiet · Kamala — small, peaceful beach · Rawai-Nai Harn — far south, good for longer stays · Phuket Old Town — Sino-Portuguese shophouses, cafes, food.

entries.name: The Surin Phuket
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Surin Beach (Pansea Bay) · cottages in a coconut grove
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this guide at 9.4 — The Surin is a boutique beach resort on Surin Beach built around privacy and a coconut-grove cottage feel. Rooms are cottages scattered across the hillside down to the beach, and Pansea Bay out front is quiet with clear water. Real guest reviews praise the attentive service and the calm setting that's still a short drive from Bang Tao.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry-level Hillside Cottages involve a fair walk up the slope — if you'd rather not climb, pick a Garden Cottage, which sits closer to the facilities and the beach.
pros: Highest score in the guide, 9.4 — attentive service
Quiet, clear-water Pansea Bay / Surin Beach, very private
Coconut-grove cottages, shaded and a world away from town
Northern location — short drive to Bang Tao/Laguna and the airport
cons: Hillside Cottages require a walk uphill — not ideal for limited mobility
Focused on quiet relaxation — not for those who want nightlife nearby

entries.name: Banyan Tree Phuket
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Tao/Laguna · every villa has a private pool
entries.addr: 33 Moo 4, Srisoonthorn Road, Cherngtalay, Thalang, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: Banyan Tree is a top-tier pool-villa resort in the Laguna Bang Tao area where every villa has its own private pool, scoring 9.2. Even the entry-level villa runs 170 square metres with a pool and outdoor pavilion. Real guest reviews consistently praise the privacy and the renowned spa. It sits within Laguna Phuket, walkable to Bang Tao Beach and the Laguna common areas.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry Banyan Pool Villa is already great value if you mainly want a private pool — save the upgrade to a Spa Pool Villa for a honeymoon when you want in-villa spa.
pros: Private pool in every villa, very generous space
Renowned spa, consistently praised in real reviews
Inside Laguna Bang Tao — quiet and private
Walkable to Bang Tao Beach and the Laguna common areas
cons: Expensive — best for a special trip or honeymoon
Large resort grounds — some points need the internal buggy

entries.name: Sri Panwa Phuket Luxury Pool Villa Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Cape Panwa · clifftop villas with sea views
entries.addr: 88 Sakdidej Road, Vichit, Mueang Phuket, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: Sri Panwa is a pool-villa resort on Cape Panwa and by far the most-reviewed hotel in this guide — over 2,615 reviews, scoring 8.9. Villas are spread across a cape jutting into the sea, with most enjoying sea views and infinity pools. It's famous for the Baba Nest bar, an iconic sunset spot. Real reviews praise the views and privacy, though some note the cape is far from town and the main beaches.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Villas sit high on the cape and rely on the resort buggy. Book the Baba Nest sunset slot well ahead — it gets very busy.
pros: Most reviewed in the guide, 2,615 reviews — iconic reputation
Clifftop villas on Cape Panwa with sea views and infinity pools
Baba Nest — the sunset spot all over social media
Very private — great for couples and groups of friends
cons: Cape Panwa is far from town and the main beaches — long drives
Villas are high on the cape — you'll depend on the internal buggy

entries.name: The Memory at On On Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phuket Old Town · Phang Nga Rd, heart of the Sino-Portuguese quarter
entries.addr: 19 Phang Nga Road, Talad Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: The Memory at On On is a heritage hotel in a Sino-Portuguese building in the heart of Phuket Old Town, and the highest-scoring pick in this guide at 9.5. The building is the original On On Hotel, once used as a filming location for The Beach. Entry rooms are compact but full of vintage character, with prices from just ฿800. Real reviews love the location — you can walk the whole Old Town: Thalang Road, cafes and street food.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Entry Superior rooms are small and some lack an external window. If you want more space and high ceilings, step up to a Deluxe or above.
pros: Highest score in the guide, 9.5 · from just ฿800
Historic Sino-Portuguese building, full of vintage character
Heart of Old Town — walk Thalang Road, cafes and street food
Best value for those who prefer Old Town over the beach
cons: Not on the beach — 30–45 minutes by car to the coast
Entry Superior rooms are small, some without an external window

entries.name: Lub d Phuket Patong
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Patong · walk to Patong Beach and Bangla Road
entries.storyHtml: Lub d Phuket Patong is a social hostel in central Patong with a big review base — 464 reviews, scoring 9.2. Its draw is the social vibe that makes it easy to meet fellow travellers, plus a pool and lively common areas. Dorms are privacy pods with curtains, plugs and reading lights, and there's a female-only dorm. Real reviews praise the location — walkable to the beach and Bangla Road.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want privacy but still the hostel buzz, book a Twin or King room — still far cheaper than a regular Patong hotel.
pros: From ฿450 — best value for backpackers in Patong
Social vibe, easy to meet fellow travellers
Pool in the hostel — rare at this price
Privacy-pod dorms with a female-only option · central Patong
cons: Patong is lively and loud — not for those wanting quiet
Common areas lean party — not ideal for families with young kids

entries.name: The Happy Eight Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rawai / Nai Harn · apartment-style rooms with kitchens
entries.addr: 79/48 Soi Samakee 5, Saiyuan Road, Rawai, Mueang, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: The Happy Eight is an apartment-style resort in the Rawai-Nai Harn area scoring a high 9.4. Its standout is that every room has a kitchen and fridge — ideal for self-catering and longer stays. Prices start from just ฿1,100, and there's a pool. Real reviews praise the value and cleanliness; the review count is still modest (51) but the scores are consistent.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rawai-Nai Harn is in the far south and not walking distance to a beach — renting a scooter or car makes getting around easier and cheaper than calling rides each time.
pros: High 9.4 score · from just ฿1,100
Every room has a kitchen and fridge — great for self-catering and long stays
Has a pool — rare at this price point
Quiet Rawai-Nai Harn area, good for relaxed longer stays
cons: Still few reviews (51) compared to others in the guide
Far south, not on the beach — a car or scooter helps

entries.name: Hotel Indigo Phuket Patong
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Patong · near Patong Beach and Jungceylon
entries.addr: 124 Rat-U-Thit 200 Pee Road, Patong, Kathu, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: Hotel Indigo Patong is a modern design hotel in central Patong with a strong 465 reviews, scoring 8.9. Entry rooms are a generous 38 square metres, with contemporary design that nods to the Patong neighbourhood. There's a pool, and it's near Patong Beach and Jungceylon mall. Real reviews praise the room size and the walkable location — a solid mid-range pick in Patong that isn't a hostel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Street-side rooms catch Patong's nightlife noise — ask for a higher floor or a Pool View room for a quieter, better outlook.
pros: Generous 38 sqm entry rooms, modern design
Plenty of reviews (465), consistent 8.9 score
Central Patong, near the beach and Jungceylon mall
Has a pool — a good mid-range option that isn't a hostel
cons: Street-side rooms catch nightlife noise — request the pool side
Patong gets crowded and traffic-heavy in high season

entries.name: Amari Phuket
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Patong (quiet end) · every room has a sea view

rooms.type: Club One Bedroom Suite Ocean View

tags: 🌊 Every room has a sea view
entries.storyHtml: Amari Phuket is a beachfront resort at the far end of Patong Beach where every room has a sea view, scoring 8.6. Its strength is the location — set on a headland away from central Patong, quieter but still close to town by foot or car. There's a seaside pool and Club rooms with Coral Lounge access. Real reviews love the balcony sea views, though some note the building is starting to show its age.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The resort sits on a slope — you can walk down to the beach but it's a climb back up. If your budget allows and you're staying several nights, a Club room with Coral Lounge access pays off.
pros: Every room has a sea view with a balcony
At the quiet end of Patong Beach on a headland
Seaside pool and Coral Lounge access for Club rooms
Still close to central Patong — good for those wanting both quiet and convenience
cons: Lowest score among the 5-star picks — the building shows its age
On a slope — you can walk to the beach but must climb back up

entries.name: KK - Karon Kata Boutique Hotel
entries.addr: 6/1 Karon Road, Karon, Mueang Phuket, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: KK - Karon Kata is the cheapest beach-area boutique hotel in this guide, from just ฿900, scoring 8.8 from 118 reviews. Rooms are clean and simple, ranging from doubles up to a Two-Bedroom Suite for groups or families. It's in the Karon-Kata area, walkable to Karon Beach and restaurants. Real reviews praise the value and the friendly staff.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a group? Book a Superior Triple or the Two-Bedroom Suite to split costs cheaply, and rent a scooter for the easy ride along Kata-Karon.
pros: From ฿900 — cheapest in the guide's beach zone
Near Karon Beach, walkable to restaurants and the sand
Triple and Two-Bedroom Suite rooms suit groups/families
Clean rooms, friendly staff · good value
cons: A small, simple hotel — limited facilities
Still few reviews (118) compared to others

entries.name: Glam Habitat
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kamala · suites with a private pool
entries.storyHtml: Glam Habitat is a Kamala-area property offering suites with a private pool from just ฿1,400, scoring 8.8 from 82 reviews. The entry room is a one-bedroom suite of around 80 square metres with a private pool, separate living area and open kitchen. Real reviews are surprised at getting a private pool for the price — ideal if you want space and privacy without paying 5-star pool-villa rates.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Kamala is a small, quiet beach and the property isn't walking distance to the sand — a car or scooter helps. Travelling as a group? The Two/Three-Bedroom units are even better value.
pros: Suites with a private pool from just ฿1,400 — surprising value
Spacious ~80 sqm entry rooms with a kitchen and separate living area
2–4 bedroom units suit groups and larger families
Quiet Kamala area, good for a private getaway
cons: Not walking distance to the beach — a car or scooter helps
Small property, still few reviews (82)

entries.name: The Old Phuket - Karon Beach Resort
entries.addr: 192/36 Karon Road, Karon, Mueang Phuket, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: The Old Phuket is a Sino-Portuguese-styled resort in the Karon Beach area, scoring 8.2 from 168 reviews. It's split into two wings — a retro Sino Wing and a modern Serene Wing — with a pool in each zone, and it's walkable to Karon Beach. Real reviews praise the decor and beach-close location, though some note that part of the rooms are showing their age, which is why it lands near the end of the guide.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Prefer retro atmosphere? Pick the Sino Wing. Want newer-looking rooms? Ask for the Serene Wing or a Deluxe Pool Access room you can step straight into the pool from.
pros: Attractive, distinctive Sino-Portuguese design
Two pool zones and Pool Access rooms
Walk to Karon Beach · family rooms available
From ฿2,000 for a beach-close resort
cons: Lowest score in the guide, 8.2 — part of the rooms show their age
Choose the wing carefully — the Sino Wing is older than the Serene Wing

entries.name: Aekkeko Hostel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phuket Old Town · walk Thalang Road and the markets
entries.addr: 55 Krabi Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: Aekkeko Hostel is the cheapest pick in this guide, from just ฿270, yet scores a high 9.3 from 419 reviews. It's in Phuket Old Town, walkable to Thalang Road, cafes and the markets. Dorms have privacy curtains, bedside plugs and large lockers, plus a female-only dorm. Real reviews praise the cleanliness and friendly staff — ideal for budget backpackers who prefer Old Town over the beach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's in Old Town, not on the beach — about 30–45 minutes by car to the coast. Want privacy on a budget? Book the Private Double room.
pros: Cheapest in the guide at ฿270 · high 9.3 score from 419 reviews
In Old Town — walk Thalang Road, cafes and markets
Curtained dorms with plugs and large lockers · female dorm available
Clean, friendly staff — great for backpackers
cons: Not on the beach — 30–45 minutes by car to the coast
It's a hostel — less privacy than a hotel

adviceTitle: How to choose the right Phuket hotel for you?

advice.head: On a budget, want the best value
advice.bodyHtml: → Aekkeko Hostel ฿270 in Old Town, scoring 9.3 · or Lub d Phuket Patong ฿450, a social hostel with a pool in central Patong

advice.head: Want to be near the nightlife, Patong
advice.bodyHtml: → Hotel Indigo Phuket Patong ฿3,800, modern design in central Patong · or Lub d Phuket Patong ฿450 on a budget

advice.head: Travelling as a family with kids
advice.bodyHtml: → The Happy Eight Resort ฿1,100 with in-room kitchens and a pool · or The Old Phuket - Karon Beach Resort ฿2,000 with family rooms near Karon Beach

advice.head: Romantic trip, couples, honeymoon
advice.bodyHtml: → Banyan Tree Phuket ฿11,500 private pool villas and a renowned spa · or The Surin Phuket ฿7,500, quiet cottages by Surin Beach

advice.head: Special trip, all-out luxury
advice.bodyHtml: → Sri Panwa Phuket ฿15,000 clifftop villas on Cape Panwa with sea views · or Banyan Tree Phuket ฿11,500 pool villas in Laguna

advice.head: Want Old Town, cafes and food
advice.bodyHtml: → The Memory at On On Hotel ฿800, a Sino-Portuguese building in the heart of Old Town, scoring 9.5 · or Aekkeko Hostel ฿270 for budget backpackers

advice.head: Want a private pool but not luxury-villa money
advice.bodyHtml: → Glam Habitat ฿1,400, suites with a private pool in Kamala · or step up to Banyan Tree Phuket if the budget allows

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Phuket hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which beach is best to stay on in Phuket?
faq.a: It depends on your style · Patong suits those who want buzz, nightlife and shopping (Hotel Indigo, Amari, Lub d) · Karon-Kata has long, quieter beaches and is family-friendly (KK, The Old Phuket) · Surin Beach / Bang Tao / Laguna is the calm luxury-resort zone (The Surin, Banyan Tree) · Phuket Old Town suits cafe-and-food lovers (The Memory at On On, Aekkeko) but isn't on the coast.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Phuket hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: hostels and budget stays start around ฿270–1,400/night · mid-range to 4-star hotels around ฿2,000–5,500 · 5-star beachfront resorts and pool villas from around ฿7,500–15,000+. All figures are indicative starting rates for standard rooms; high season (Nov–Apr) runs well above normal.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Phuket hotel?
faq.a: For weekdays outside peak season, 2–4 weeks ahead is enough · but in high season (November–April), especially New Year and Songkran, good rooms and beachfront resorts sell out fast — book 1–2 months ahead or more.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get around between beaches in Phuket?
faq.a: Phuket has no metro and limited public transport. Getting around means a rental car, scooter, taxi or Grab (Grab can be hard to hail and pricier than in big cities). Distances between beaches are further than expected — Patong to Kata is about 20–30 minutes, Old Town to the beach about 30–45 minutes. If you plan to visit several beaches, having a car or scooter is more convenient and cheaper.

faq.q: ❓ Should I stay by the beach or in Old Town?
faq.a: By the beach (Patong, Karon-Kata, Surin, Bang Tao) suits trips focused on swimming, the sand and sea views · Phuket Old Town suits those who love Sino-Portuguese architecture, cafes and local food — but it's a 30–45 minute drive to the beach. On a longer trip, splitting your stay between both gives you two very different vibes.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book Phuket hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so we recommend comparing all 3 before every booking — each review page in this guide includes price-comparison links, which can save hundreds to over a thousand baht per night in peak periods.
